(C) **GREEN, exit 0, all 10 PASS** — blind spot 1. guards.note: Blind spot 1 is lesson 2, and the mirror image of batch 5's deep-zoom-la: there every fixture sat on the real axis so imaginary errors were unreachable; here every fixture is a phase-0 sine, odd about i=0, and the periodic Hann window is even about it - so the windowed frame is odd and its transform purely imaginary (measured max|Re| 9.2e-6 vs max|Im| 5.1e+2 at N=2048). Blind spot 2 is an unasserted public contract two other modules depend on. Margins: block [4] runs at 3.7e-7 dB against a 0.15 dB tolerance; block [3] at 166 dB against >30, loose and deliberately NOT tightened - 166 dB is the float32 noise floor, and its comment's claim that it catches a missing window is wrong (a rectangular window leaks nothing for an on-bin tone). Block [4]'s 6 dB shift catches that.

guards.break: Six breaks in engine/features/audioMod/bandMath.ts, each reverted. Controls: unit-sum kernel normalisation removed; the Hann weight replaced by a rectangular 1; TILT_REF_HZ moved to 1000. Probes: (P) `resolutionLimited` -> `false`; (P3) -> `true`; (Q) `fMax` -> `nyquist`; (Q3) -> `Math.min(BANK_MAX_HZ, nyquist)`.
guards.result: Controls RED: no normalisation exit 1 (worst 140.76); rectangular kernel exit 1 on the edge-to-centre shape; TILT_REF_HZ exit 1 on two assertions. BEFORE repair: (P) **GREEN** - every band unflagged, message printing '(0 of 56)' while passing; (Q) **GREEN** - the bank ran to 22807 Hz, 6.8 kHz above the declared ceiling. AFTER: (P) 4 FAIL, (P3) 4 FAIL, (Q) 2 FAIL, (Q3) 1 FAIL - so the 0.95 nyquist guard is now covered separately from BANK_MAX_HZ.
guards.verdict: healthy on kernels and tilt; two measured blind spots on the resolution flag and the band ceiling (both repaired)
guards.note: (P) is the fifth failure mode one level down - not a vanished INPUT but a vanished RESULT SET. `flagged.length ? Math.max(...) : 0` means 'no bands flagged' scores 0, and 0 is under every limit, so the emptier the answer the safer it looks. (Q) is lesson 4: the assertion existed but its threshold was 9.6 kHz slacker than the contract it stood in for. The nyquist half needed a second sample rate to be testable at all - measured across nine rates, 32/44.1/48 kHz cannot discriminate `nyquist` from `nyquist * 0.95` because BANK_MAX_HZ binds first; 24000 and 12000 are the only two that can.

guards.note: Lesson 2 twice in one fixture. Every frame index was 120 and the only ratio was 0.5, so (i) the keyframe and the deck-0 clip carried the same number with the same expectation at all six steps, and (ii) 120 x 0.5 = 60 exactly, so rounding never bound. A deck-1 clip at 91 is distinct from every keyframe and odd, fixing both; it deliberately does NOT round-trip (46 x 2 = 92) and is asserted at 92 rather than dropped. CRLF WILL SILENTLY VOID A BREAK. Working files here are CRLF, so `perl -0pi` patterns containing \n and `perl -pi` patterns anchored with ^ or $ match nothing and exit 0 - the guard appears to pass a break that was never applied. Two false blind-spot readings came from this. Confirm every break with `git diff --stat`, or use the Edit tool.
